    A guide to single-cell plotting functions¶

    Python port of the R vignette A guide to single-cell plotting functions. Original author: Liesbeth François.

    Intro¶

    This vignette gives an overview of the different plotting functions that are available when running a single cell analysis. The plots live in bv.pl and need matplotlib (the plots extra); the extract_* functions next to them return the data behind each plot as a polars frame.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

import bixverse as bv
import bixverse.embed
from bixverse.params import NeighboursParams
    import tempfile from pathlib import Path from typing import Literal import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import polars as pl import bixverse as bv import bixverse.embed from bixverse.params import NeighboursParams

    Preparing the data¶

    We run the standard analysis using the same PBMC3k data set. For more details on the data analysis itself, please refer to the PBMC vignette. This vignette assumes familiarity with how the SingleCells class, on-disk storage and cells-to-keep logic work. To have something to group the QC by, every cell gets a random sample label.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    pbmc3k_path = bv.io.download_pbmc3k()

tempdir_pbmc = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

sc = bv.io.load_mtx(
    Path(tempdir_pbmc.name) / "pbmc3k",
    bv.io.get_cell_ranger_params(pbmc3k_path),
    verbose=True,
)

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"sample": rng.choice(["sample1", "sample2"], sc.n_cells)}))

sc.rename_var_col("column1", "gene_symbol")

var = sc.var()

ensembl_to_symbol = dict(zip(var["gene_id"], var["gene_symbol"], strict=True))
symbol_to_ensembl = dict(zip(var["gene_symbol"], var["gene_id"], strict=True))

scrublet_res = bv.doublets.scrublet(sc)

sc.add_obs(bv.doublets.get_data(scrublet_res))

cells_without_doublets = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "doublet"]).filter(~pl.col("doublet"))[
    "cell_id"
]

sc.set_cells_to_keep(cells_without_doublets.to_list())

# define gene sets whose proportional expression signals low quality
gs_of_interest = {
    "MT": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^MT-"))["gene_id"].to_list(),
    "Ribo": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^RP[SL]"))[
        "gene_id"
    ].to_list(),
}

bv.qc.gene_set_proportions(sc, gs_of_interest, streaming=False, verbose=True)

# collect metrics for outlier detection
qc_df = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "sample", "lib_size", "nnz", "MT"], filtered=True)

metrics = {
    "log10_lib_size": np.log10(qc_df["lib_size"].to_numpy()),
    "log10_nnz": np.log10(qc_df["nnz"].to_numpy()),
    "MT": qc_df["MT"].to_numpy(),
}

directions: dict[str, Literal["twosided", "below", "above"]] = {
    "log10_lib_size": "twosided",
    "log10_nnz": "twosided",
    "MT": "above",
}

qc = bv.qc.run_cell_qc(
    metrics,
    sc.cells_to_keep,
    directions=directions,
    threshold=3.0,
    groups=qc_df["sample"],
)
    pbmc3k_path = bv.io.download_pbmc3k() tempdir_pbmc = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() sc = bv.io.load_mtx( Path(tempdir_pbmc.name) / "pbmc3k", bv.io.get_cell_ranger_params(pbmc3k_path), verbose=True, ) rng = np.random.default_rng(42) sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"sample": rng.choice(["sample1", "sample2"], sc.n_cells)})) sc.rename_var_col("column1", "gene_symbol") var = sc.var() ensembl_to_symbol = dict(zip(var["gene_id"], var["gene_symbol"], strict=True)) symbol_to_ensembl = dict(zip(var["gene_symbol"], var["gene_id"], strict=True)) scrublet_res = bv.doublets.scrublet(sc) sc.add_obs(bv.doublets.get_data(scrublet_res)) cells_without_doublets = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "doublet"]).filter(~pl.col("doublet"))[ "cell_id" ] sc.set_cells_to_keep(cells_without_doublets.to_list()) # define gene sets whose proportional expression signals low quality gs_of_interest = { "MT": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^MT-"))["gene_id"].to_list(), "Ribo": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^RP[SL]"))[ "gene_id" ].to_list(), } bv.qc.gene_set_proportions(sc, gs_of_interest, streaming=False, verbose=True) # collect metrics for outlier detection qc_df = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "sample", "lib_size", "nnz", "MT"], filtered=True) metrics = { "log10_lib_size": np.log10(qc_df["lib_size"].to_numpy()), "log10_nnz": np.log10(qc_df["nnz"].to_numpy()), "MT": qc_df["MT"].to_numpy(), } directions: dict[str, Literal["twosided", "below", "above"]] = { "log10_lib_size": "twosided", "log10_nnz": "twosided", "MT": "above", } qc = bv.qc.run_cell_qc( metrics, sc.cells_to_keep, directions=directions, threshold=3.0, groups=qc_df["sample"], )

    Joint QC plot¶

    joint_plot() compares the number of features and number of counts per cell, similar to sns.jointplot.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.joint_plot(qc)
plt.show()
    bv.pl.joint_plot(qc) plt.show()

    Violin QC plots¶

    violin_plot() shows the distribution of each QC metric as a violin, split by sample (or any grouping variable stored in the qc object).

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.violin_plot(qc, group_name="sample")
plt.show()
    bv.pl.violin_plot(qc, group_name="sample") plt.show()

    Alternatively, we can also provide a frame and generate the violin plots with different variables than those considered in the QC.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    obs = sc.obs(filtered=True)

bv.pl.violin_plot(
    obs,
    grouping_column="sample",
    variable="Ribo",
    show_outlier=True,
)
plt.show()
    obs = sc.obs(filtered=True) bv.pl.violin_plot( obs, grouping_column="sample", variable="Ribo", show_outlier=True, ) plt.show()

    Density QC plots¶

    density_plot() overlays smoothed density distributions for each group, which highlights bimodal distributions or outlier populations that violins can obscure.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.density_plot(qc)
plt.show()
    bv.pl.density_plot(qc) plt.show()

    Dimensionality reduction plots¶

    After PCA, neighbour-finding, clustering and UMAP, cells can be visualised on any 2D embedding stored in the object. The scType annotation from the PBMC vignette gives us cell types to colour by.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000, verbose=True)

bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30, sparse_svd=True)

# the data is so tiny that exhaustive kNN search is faster than building
# an approximate nearest neighbour index
bv.graph.find_neighbours(
    sc, neighbours_params=NeighboursParams(knn_method="exhaustive")
)

bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=0.5, name="leiden_clusters")

bv.embed.umap(sc)

cell_markers = {
    "CD3D": "T cells",
    "CD3E": "T cells",
    "CD3G": "T cells",
    "IL7R": "CD4+ T",
    "CD4": "CD4+ T",
    "CD8A": "CD8+ T",
    "CD8B": "CD8+ T",
    "MS4A1": "B cells",
    "CD79A": "B cells",
    "CD19": "B cells",
    "CD14": "CD14+ Mono",
    "LYZ": "CD14+ Mono",
    "S100A8": "CD14+ Mono",
    "FCGR3A": "CD16+ Mono",
    "CDKN1C": "CD16+ Mono",
    "GNLY": "NK",
    "NKG7": "NK",
    "NCAM1": "NK",
    "FCER1A": "mDC",
    "CD1C": "mDC",
    "LILRA4": "pDC",
    "CLEC4C": "pDC",
    "PPBP": "Platelet",
    "PF4": "Platelet",
}

cell_markers_df = pl.DataFrame(
    {"gene_symbol": list(cell_markers), "cell_type": list(cell_markers.values())}
).join(var.select("gene_symbol", "gene_id"), on="gene_symbol")

# prepare the list of markers
marker_list = bv.annotate.prepare_cell_markers(sc, cell_markers_df)
# calculate the score for each cell
sctype_scores = bv.annotate.calc_sc_type_scores(sc, marker_list)
# annotate the clusters
leiden = sc.obs(cols=["leiden_clusters"], filtered=True)["leiden_clusters"]
cell_type_anno = bv.annotate.score_clusters(sctype_scores, leiden.to_numpy())

sc.add_obs(
    sc.obs(cols=["cell_idx", "leiden_clusters"], filtered=True)
    .join(
        cell_type_anno.select(
            pl.col("cluster_id").alias("leiden_clusters"),
            pl.col("cell_type").alias("sc_type"),
        ),
        on="leiden_clusters",
        how="left",
    )
    .select("cell_idx", "sc_type")
)
    bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000, verbose=True) bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30, sparse_svd=True) # the data is so tiny that exhaustive kNN search is faster than building # an approximate nearest neighbour index bv.graph.find_neighbours( sc, neighbours_params=NeighboursParams(knn_method="exhaustive") ) bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=0.5, name="leiden_clusters") bv.embed.umap(sc) cell_markers = { "CD3D": "T cells", "CD3E": "T cells", "CD3G": "T cells", "IL7R": "CD4+ T", "CD4": "CD4+ T", "CD8A": "CD8+ T", "CD8B": "CD8+ T", "MS4A1": "B cells", "CD79A": "B cells", "CD19": "B cells", "CD14": "CD14+ Mono", "LYZ": "CD14+ Mono", "S100A8": "CD14+ Mono", "FCGR3A": "CD16+ Mono", "CDKN1C": "CD16+ Mono", "GNLY": "NK", "NKG7": "NK", "NCAM1": "NK", "FCER1A": "mDC", "CD1C": "mDC", "LILRA4": "pDC", "CLEC4C": "pDC", "PPBP": "Platelet", "PF4": "Platelet", } cell_markers_df = pl.DataFrame( {"gene_symbol": list(cell_markers), "cell_type": list(cell_markers.values())} ).join(var.select("gene_symbol", "gene_id"), on="gene_symbol") # prepare the list of markers marker_list = bv.annotate.prepare_cell_markers(sc, cell_markers_df) # calculate the score for each cell sctype_scores = bv.annotate.calc_sc_type_scores(sc, marker_list) # annotate the clusters leiden = sc.obs(cols=["leiden_clusters"], filtered=True)["leiden_clusters"] cell_type_anno = bv.annotate.score_clusters(sctype_scores, leiden.to_numpy()) sc.add_obs( sc.obs(cols=["cell_idx", "leiden_clusters"], filtered=True) .join( cell_type_anno.select( pl.col("cluster_id").alias("leiden_clusters"), pl.col("cell_type").alias("sc_type"), ), on="leiden_clusters", how="left", ) .select("cell_idx", "sc_type") )

plt.show()

    sc,
    "umap",
    "sc_type",
    label_by="leiden_clusters",

plt.show()

    "umap",
    "Ribo",
    discrete=False,
    point_alpha=0.2,

plt.show()
    bv.pl.embedding_plot( sc, "umap", "Ribo", discrete=False, point_alpha=0.2, ) plt.show()

    Key arguments:

    Argument Description
    embedding Name of the stored embedding ("umap", "tsne", "pca", ...)
    colour_by Metadata column used to colour points
    label_by Metadata column used to label centroids
    discrete True for categorical palettes, False for continuous
    point_alpha Transparency (0 to 1); reduce for dense data sets
    ax matplotlib axes to draw on, for multi-panel figures

    Other 2D embeddings¶

    UMAP is not the only game in town. All the 2D embeddings come from manifolds-rs and land in the same object, so embedding_plot() works on every one of them.

    Density-preserving embeddings¶

    UMAP and t-SNE throw away local density. A tight, homogeneous population and a diffuse, heterogeneous one come out at roughly the same size, so reading anything into the area a cluster takes up on the plot is a mistake. densMAP and den-SNE fix this with an extra term in the loss that keeps the local radius of each cell in the embedding correlated with its radius in PCA space. Big blob now means lots of variation, small tight blob means not much. lambda_ on bv.embed.densmap_defaults() and bv.embed.densne_defaults() sets how hard that term pulls; lambda_=0 gives you plain UMAP and t-SNE back.

    The t-SNE flavours come with four optimisers via approx: "barnes_hut" (classic Barnes-Hut), "qd" (the quick-and-dirty Barnes-Hut of qdtsne, tree depth capped via max_depth on the optimiser parameters, coarser by design), "fft" (FIt-SNE style interpolation) and "fft_3k" (its three-kernel variant). Here we use "fft_3k". The estimators are sklearn style, so set_params swaps the optimiser on the defaults.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    bv.embed.densmap(sc)
bv.embed.tsne(sc, params=bv.embed.tsne_defaults().set_params(approx="fft_3k"))  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type] # manifolds-rs types set_params as BaseEmbedding
bv.embed.densne(sc, params=bv.embed.densne_defaults().set_params(approx="fft_3k"))  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type] # manifolds-rs types set_params as BaseEmbedding
    bv.embed.densmap(sc) bv.embed.tsne(sc, params=bv.embed.tsne_defaults().set_params(approx="fft_3k")) # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type] # manifolds-rs types set_params as BaseEmbedding bv.embed.densne(sc, params=bv.embed.densne_defaults().set_params(approx="fft_3k")) # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type] # manifolds-rs types set_params as BaseEmbedding

    UMAP and t-SNE (left) next to their density-preserving versions (right), coloured by cell type. Every plot takes an ax, so a grid is just plt.subplots.

    In [13]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 10), layout="constrained")

for ax, embd in zip(axes.flat, ["umap", "densmap", "tsne", "densne"], strict=True):
    bv.pl.embedding_plot(sc, embd, "sc_type", discrete=True, ax=ax)
    ax.set_title(embd)

plt.show()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 10), layout="constrained") for ax, embd in zip(axes.flat, ["umap", "densmap", "tsne", "densne"], strict=True): bv.pl.embedding_plot(sc, embd, "sc_type", discrete=True, ax=ax) ax.set_title(embd) plt.show()

    ForceAtlas2¶

    ForceAtlas2 is a force-directed layout of the neighbour graph: edges pull, every pair of cells pushes, gravity keeps the lot together. It is what scanpy's draw_graph() does, and a common pick for data with continuous transitions (think differentiation). bv.embed.forceatlas2() lays out the kNN graph the same way scanpy does.

    Not ported to Python yet: the layout of the neighbour graph the Leiden clustering ran on (R's graph = "connectivities"), the manifolds-rs wheel cannot lay out a given graph.

    In [14]:
    Copied! 
    bv.embed.forceatlas2(sc)

bv.pl.embedding_plot(sc, "fa2", "sc_type", discrete=True)
plt.show()
    bv.embed.forceatlas2(sc) bv.pl.embedding_plot(sc, "fa2", "sc_type", discrete=True) plt.show()

    Per-gene expression plots¶

    feature_plot() projects normalised expression of one or more genes onto the embedding. Here MS4A1: the high-expressing cells sit in the B cell cluster, as they should.

    In [15]:
    Copied! 
    features = [symbol_to_ensembl[s] for s in cell_markers if s in symbol_to_ensembl]
feature_labels = {f: ensembl_to_symbol[f] for f in features}

ms4a1 = symbol_to_ensembl["MS4A1"]

bv.pl.feature_plot(
    sc,
    [ms4a1],
    "umap",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
    label_by="sc_type",
)
plt.show()
    features = [symbol_to_ensembl[s] for s in cell_markers if s in symbol_to_ensembl] feature_labels = {f: ensembl_to_symbol[f] for f in features} ms4a1 = symbol_to_ensembl["MS4A1"] bv.pl.feature_plot( sc, [ms4a1], "umap", feature_labels=feature_labels, label_by="sc_type", ) plt.show()

    Tip: pass a list of Ensembl IDs to features and a matching feature_labels dict to produce one panel per gene.

    We can also highlight the genes of interest for clearer visualisation.

    In [16]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.feature_plot(
    sc,
    [ms4a1],
    "umap",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
    label_by="sc_type",
    highlight_features=True,
)
plt.show()
    bv.pl.feature_plot( sc, [ms4a1], "umap", feature_labels=feature_labels, label_by="sc_type", highlight_features=True, ) plt.show()

    Dot plots¶

    Dot plots encode two dimensions simultaneously:

    • Dot size: fraction of cells in the group expressing the gene (at least one count)
    • Dot colour: mean (scaled) expression over all cells of the group, zeros included
    In [18]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.dot_plot(
    sc,
    features,
    "leiden_clusters",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
    scale_exp=True,
    # keyed by the display label, here the symbol
    feature_grouping=cell_markers,
    cluster_groups=True,
)
plt.show()
    bv.pl.dot_plot( sc, features, "leiden_clusters", feature_labels=feature_labels, scale_exp=True, # keyed by the display label, here the symbol feature_grouping=cell_markers, cluster_groups=True, ) plt.show()

    Key arguments:

    Argument Description
    features Ensembl IDs to plot
    feature_labels Display names shown on the axis
    grouping_variable Cell metadata column defining rows
    scale_exp Min-max scale the group means per gene
    feature_grouping Dict mapping gene to group label for the x-axis brackets
    cluster_groups Hierarchically cluster rows by expression profile

    Extracting the plotting data

    Alternatively, you can also extract the plotting data directly to make customised plots.

    In [19]:
    Copied! 
    df = bv.pl.extract_dot_plot_data(sc, features, "leiden_clusters")

    Heatmaps¶

    Dot plots summarise each group. Want to see every single cell instead? The marker heatmap puts genes on the rows and cells on the columns, with a gap between clusters. Expression is z-scored per gene and clipped at 2.5 by default, otherwise a few extreme cells eat the whole colour range.

    In [20]:
    Copied! 
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5), layout="constrained")

bv.pl.heatmap_plot(
    sc,
    features,
    "leiden_clusters",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
    feature_grouping=cell_markers,
    ax=ax,
)
plt.show()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5), layout="constrained") bv.pl.heatmap_plot( sc, features, "leiden_clusters", feature_labels=feature_labels, feature_grouping=cell_markers, ax=ax, ) plt.show()

    Big clusters hog the width and the platelets end up as a sliver. max_cells_per_group subsamples every group, which gives the small ones a fair share of the plot.

    In [21]:
    Copied! 
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5), layout="constrained")

bv.pl.heatmap_plot(
    sc,
    features,
    "sc_type",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
    feature_grouping=cell_markers,
    max_cells_per_group=100,
    ax=ax,
)
plt.show()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5), layout="constrained") bv.pl.heatmap_plot( sc, features, "sc_type", feature_labels=feature_labels, feature_grouping=cell_markers, max_cells_per_group=100, ax=ax, ) plt.show()

    The data behind it comes from extract_gene_expression(), in case you want to build your own.

    Stacked violin plots¶

    Stacked violins show the per-group expression distribution of several genes in a compact vertical layout.

    In [22]:
    Copied! 
    # take the first five markers
bv.pl.stacked_violin_plot(
    sc,
    features[:5],
    "sc_type",
    feature_labels=feature_labels,
)
plt.show()
    # take the first five markers bv.pl.stacked_violin_plot( sc, features[:5], "sc_type", feature_labels=feature_labels, ) plt.show()
